questions.stem: When a car brakes to a stop, what happens to its kinetic energy?

options.text: It is transferred to thermal energy in the brakes and surroundings
It remains as kinetic energy in the brakes
It is converted to gravitational potential energy

questions.explanation: When brakes are applied, friction between the brake pads and discs converts the car's kinetic energy into thermal energy. The brakes, tyres, and road all heat up. Energy is never destroyed, only transferred to other stores.
